source_text: ἀποστολὴ, πλὴν εἰς βασιλείαν καὶ δόξαν. Τελειοῖ γὰρ οὕτως τὸν Ἀαρὼν, χρυσοῦν ἐπὶ τῷ μετώπῳ τὸ ψαλίον τιθείς. Κύριος δὲ τῶν ὅλων καὶ βασιλεὺς, ὁ Χριστὸς, φυσικῶς τε ἅμα καὶ μεθεκτῶς. Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν φύσει κεκένωκεν ἑαυτὸν, καθεὶς ἐν δούλου μορφῇ. Καὶ δέχεται βασιλείαν, κατά γε τὸ πρέπον τῷ ἀνθρωπίνῳ σχήματι, καίτοι σύνεδρος ὢν ἄνωθέν τε καὶ ἀπ' ἀρχῆς τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, καὶ συγκατάρχων τῶν ὅλων καὶ συνδεσπότης. Σύνες δὲ ὅπως ἐξ ὑακίνθου γέγονεν ἡ μίτρα αὐτοῦ, τὸ λαμπρὸν τῆς βασιλείας ἔχουσα σύνθημα, φημὶ δὴ τὸ πέταλον τὸ χρυσοῦν. Ὑάκινθος δὲ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖον· καὶ διαμέμνησο λέγοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, «Ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.» Οὐ γὰρ ἐπίγειος βασιλεὺς, ἀλλ' οὐράνιος ὁ Χριστὸς, ὅλην ὑπὸ πόδας ἔχων τὴν κτίσιν. Προσεπενεγκὼν δὲ, ὅτι «Καὶ ἐξαρεῖ Ἀαρὼν τὰ ἁμαρτήματα τῶν ἁγίων ὅσα ἂν ἁγιάσωσι, παντὸς δόματος τῶν ἁγίων αὐτῶν,» ὅτι πᾶσά τε προσαγωγὴ καὶ τελείωσις ἐν Χριστῷ, διαμεμήνυκεν ἐναργῶς, καὶ μὴν ὅτι πᾶσα δικαίωσις ἐν αὐτῷ τε καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἡ τῶν πάλαι πλημμελημάτων ἀπόθεσις. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἡμῶν αἴρει τὰς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ γεγόναμεν δεκτοὶ, τὰς ἐν πνεύματι δωροφορίας προσκομίζοντες τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀναπόθετον δὲ καὶ διηνεκῆ καὶ εἰς ἀπεράντους αἰῶνας ἐκτεινομένην τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν βασιλείαν εὖ μάλα καταδεικνὺς, περί τε τῆς μίτρας τοῦ πετάλου φησί· «Καὶ ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου Ἀαρὼν διὰ παντός.» Εἶτα ποῖ ποτ' ἂν ἡμῖν ὁ θρασὺς καὶ ἀπόπληκτος τῶν ἀνοσίων αἱρετικῶν οἰχήσεται λόγος, πεφλυαρηκότων ὅτι καταλήξει ποτὲ τὸ Χριστοῦ κράτος, καὶ παραδώσει τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, τῶν τῆς θεότητος ἀποφοιτήσας θώκων ὁ Ἐμμανουήλ; Ἐπισεμνύνονται γὰρ τοῖς ὧδε δεινοῖς καὶ ἐξιτήλοις δόγμασιν, οἷς ἀκόλουθον εἰπεῖν· «Πλανᾶσθε, μὴ εἰδότες τὰς Γραφάς.» Ἰδοὺ γὰρ, ἰδοὺ σαφῶς τε καὶ ἐναργῶς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ διηνεκεῖ, καὶ τοῖς τῆς βασιλείας συνθήμασι ταινιοῦντος τὸν Ἀαρὼν, ἀποστεφανοῦσιν αὐτοὶ, καὶ μονονουχὶ τοῖς μετώποις ἐμπρέπουσαν τὴν ἱερὰν ἁρπάζουσι μίτραν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} «Κίδαρίν τε καὶ ζώνην ἐκ βύσσου ποιήσεις,» φησί. Στρατιωτικὸν δὲ τῷ Ἀαρὼν τὸ σχῆμα, ζωστήρ τε καὶ κράνος· ἐν εἴδει γάρ πως ἡ κίδαρις τῷ τοιῷδέ ἐστι. Πεπολέμηκε γὰρ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὁ Χριστὸς «ἐν χειρὶ κρυφαίᾳ,» κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καὶ «Τὸ τόξον αὐτοῦ ἐνέτεινε, καὶ ἡτοίμασεν αὐτὸ, τὰ βέλη αὐτοῦ τοῖς καιομένοις ἐξειργάσατο,» καὶ καθεῖλεν ἀρχὰς, τεθριάμβευκε δυνάμεις, κατέσεισε κυριότητας, καὶ αἰχμαλώτους ὄντας ἐῤῥύσατο τοὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Ὅτι δὲ οὐχ ὁρατὸς ἢ παχὺς ὁ πόλεμος, οὐδὲ οἷον πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα, γέγονεν αὐτῷ, ὑποφαίνειν ἔοικεν αἰνιγματωδῶς τὸ ἐκ βύσσου μόνης τῆς ἄγαν
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing §11: 'a showing-forth into this world and'] sending (ἀποστολή), but into kingship (βασιλεία) and glory (δόξα). For thus he perfects (τελειόω) Aaron, setting the golden band (ψαλίον) on the forehead. And Lord of all things (τῶν ὅλων) and king is Christ, both naturally (φυσικῶς) and by participation (μεθεκτῶς). For being God by nature he has emptied (κενόω) himself, letting himself down (καθίημι) into a slave's form (δούλου μορφή). And he receives kingship according to what befits the human form (ἀνθρώπινον σχῆμα), although being co-seated (σύνεδρος) from above and from the beginning with God and Father, and co-ruling (συγκατάρχω) all things and co-master (συνδεσπότης). Understand how his mitre is of hyacinth, having the bright token (σύνθημα) of kingship, I mean the golden plate. Hyacinth a sign (σημεῖον) of heaven; and remember Christ saying: 'My kingdom is not from this world.' For Christ is not an earthly (ἐπίγειος) but a heavenly (οὐράνιος) king, having the whole creation under feet. And having added: 'And Aaron will take away the sins of the holy things, as many as they sanctify, of every gift of their holy things,' he has clearly indicated (διαμηνύω) that every bringing-near/access (προσαγωγή) and perfecting (τελείωσις) is in Christ, and indeed that all justification (δικαίωσις) is in him and through him, and the putting away (ἀπόθεσις) of the old offences (πλημμελήματα). For he takes away (αἴρω) our sins, and through him we have become acceptable (δεκτοί), bringing (προσκομίζω) the gift-offerings in spirit (αἱ ἐν πνεύματι δωροφορίαι) to God and Father. Pall.: You spoke well. Cyr.: And showing very well that the kingship of our Saviour is not to be laid aside (ἀναπόθετος) and continual (διηνεκής) and extending into unbounded (ἀπέραντος) ages, he says concerning the plate of the mitre: 'And it will be on Aaron's forehead continually.' Then where ever will the bold (θρασύς) and stricken-witless (ἀπόπληκτος) account of the unholy (ἀνόσιος) heretics go, who have babbled (φλυαρέω) that Christ's might (κράτος) will one day cease (καταλήγω), and that Emmanuel will hand over (παραδίδωμι) the kingdom to God and Father, having departed from (ἀποφοιτάω) the seats (θῶκοι) of the Godhead (θεότης)? For they pride themselves (ἐπισεμνύνομαι) on such terrible and fading (ἐξίτηλος) doctrines, to whom it follows to say: 'You err (πλανᾶσθε), not knowing the Scriptures.' For behold, behold, while the God and Father clearly and plainly binds Aaron with a fillet (ταινιόω) with glory and continual honour (τιμή) and the tokens of kingship, they themselves uncrown (ἀποστεφανόω) [him], and all but snatch (ἁρπάζω) the holy mitre that is conspicuous (ἐμπρέπω) on the foreheads. Pall.: True. Cyr.: 'You shall make a headdress (κίδαρις) and a belt (ζώνη) of fine linen (βύσσος),' he says. Military (στρατιωτικός) is Aaron's figure (σχῆμα), belt (ζωστήρ) and helmet (κράνος); for the headdress is somehow in the form of such. For Christ has warred (πολεμέω) for us 'with a hidden hand (χεὶρ κρυφαία),' according to what is written, and 'He stretched (ἐντείνω) his bow and prepared it, his arrows (βέλη) he worked out (ἐξεργάζομαι) for those being burned (καιόμενοι),' and he pulled down (καθαιρέω) rulers (ἀρχαί), has triumphed over (θριαμβεύω) powers (δυνάμεις), shook down (κατασείω) lordships (κυριότητες), and rescued (ῥύομαι) those on earth being captives (αἰχμάλωτοι). And that the war has not become for him visible (ὁρατός) or thick/gross (παχύς), nor as toward blood and flesh, the making of the war-gear from fine linen alone, the very [continues §13: thin, headdress and belt] seems to indicate in a riddle (αἰνιγματωδῶς).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …a sending, yet for kingship and glory. For in this way he brings Aaron to completion, setting the golden band on his forehead. And Christ is Lord and King of all, both by nature and by participation. For though he is God by nature, he emptied himself, lowering himself into the form of a servant (Philippians 2:7); and he receives kingship in the way that befits his human form, even though from above and from the beginning he sits beside God the Father, rules all things with him and is Master of all with him. Notice how his turban is made of blue and bears the bright token of kingship, I mean the golden plate. Blue is a sign of heaven; and remember that Christ says, ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ (John 18:36). For Christ is not an earthly king but a heavenly one, having the whole creation under his feet (Ephesians 1:22). And by adding, ‘And Aaron shall take away the sins of the holy things, whatever they consecrate, of every gift of their holy things’ (Exodus 28:38), he has clearly shown that all access and all perfecting are in Christ, and indeed that all justification is in him and through him, and also the putting away of former offenses. For he takes away our sins (John 1:29), and through him we have become acceptable, bringing offerings in spirit to God the Father (1 Peter 2:5).

Cyril: And showing very well that our Savior’s kingship cannot be laid aside, but is continual and stretches into endless ages, he says of the plate on the turban, ‘And it shall be on Aaron’s forehead continually’ (Exodus 28:38). What then will become of the bold and senseless talk of the unholy heretics, who have babbled that Christ’s dominion will one day come to an end, and that Emmanuel will hand over the kingdom to God the Father (1 Corinthians 15:24) and leave the thrones of the Godhead? For they pride themselves on doctrines so dreadful and so short-lived; and it is fitting to say to them, ‘You are wrong, because you do not know the Scriptures’ (Matthew 22:29). For look, look: while God the Father plainly and clearly crowns Aaron with lasting glory and honor and with the tokens of kingship, they take the crown from him, and all but snatch away the sacred turban that graces his forehead.

Cyril: ‘And you shall make a headdress and a belt of fine linen’ (Exodus 28:39), he says. Aaron’s dress is that of a soldier, a belt and a helmet; for the headdress is shaped rather like a helmet. For Christ has fought for us ‘with a hidden hand’ (Exodus 17:16), as it is written; and ‘he has bent his bow and made it ready; he has fashioned his arrows for those who are burning’ (Psalm 7:12–13); and he has pulled down rulers, led powers in triumph (Colossians 2:15), shaken dominions, and rescued those on earth who were captives.
